supplement.holds: The paper says detailed case-study data and experimental materials are in Supplementary Information (p. 18). Main-text pointers include productivity/experience results in Supplementary Figures 9-13 (p. 10), creativity details in Supplementary Figures 21-22 (p. 12), moral-reasoning analyses in Supplementary Tables 2-3 and Supplementary Figure 33 (p. 12), and a user manual in Supplementary Section G (p. 18). The absent supplement has not been inspected, so its participant counts, exact estimators, and availability of means, SDs, or SEs cannot be confirmed.

paper_design_summary: The paper reports three Epitome case studies: management professionals assigned to ChatGPT or Overleaf for writing assessed by experts for writing quality, content quality, and originality (pp. 9-10); a randomized adventure-story task with zero, one, or five AI ideas and creativity/diversity outcomes in English and Chinese (pp. 10-12); and a moral-reasoning study combining AI simulation with human-AI courtroom role-play (pp. 12-14). The writing studies test assistance to humans, rather than separately generated AI versus human work, while the courtroom study is outside the creativity scope.

studies.label: Case Study 2: adventure-story creativity and diversity (Doshi and Hauser replication)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Participants were assigned between subjects to human-only writing, one AI-generated suggestion, or five AI-generated suggestions. English and Chinese conditions are reported, but the main PDF does not establish whether they use independent samples or how language was assigned. Online classification follows the Epitome survey/chat workflow; the recruitment source and physical testing location are not stated.
assignment.quote: In this experiment, participants were randomly assigned to one of three groups: a control group (Human-only), a group with one AI-generated suggestion, and a group with five AI-generated suggestions.

eligibility.reason: Case Study 2 explicitly randomizes people to zero, one, or five AI suggestions and scores their adventure stories, satisfying assignment and output criteria (p. 11, Fig. 3 caption; p. 12, creativity/diversity results). It does not state the number of people analyzed: Fig. 3a labels 31 stories, an output count, and the reported test degrees of freedom do not establish a participant count. Thus the at-least-50-people criterion cannot be confirmed. Case Study 1 has 35 people analyzed and independently fails the size threshold (p. 9, Fig. 2 caption). Case Study 3 concerns moral reasoning rather than creative output (pp. 12-13, Fig. 4). The absent Supplementary Information may resolve the story sample and analysis details (p. 18).

one_line_finding: The story-writing replication reports individual-creativity increases of 42.1% with one AI idea and 16.4% with five, alongside a 5.64%-6.47% decline in collective diversity, but does not state the analyzed participant count (p. 12, Human creativity and generative AI; p. 11, Fig. 3).
open_questions: How many people were randomized and analyzed in each story-writing arm and language, and what does the 31 stories label in Fig. 3a cover? The main text does not establish the size criterion.
Do the English and Chinese conditions use separate samples, or are they language conditions within one sample? They are retained as one case-study entry until this can be established.

Obtain the cited Supplementary Information and Reporting Summary to verify exclusions, recruitment, scoring scales, rater numbers, arm-level statistics, and whether the t-tests account for repeated outputs or ratings.

What are the collective-diversity metric and comparison sets, and which arms/languages correspond to 5.64%-6.47%, t = 5.52, and t = 54.80? The printed p < 0.05 and df = 28 are not clearly allocated to both tests.

How do the three expert-rated dimensions relate to the headline output-quality and individual-creativity results? The available PDF does not define the composites or supply separate dimension results.
Confirm the saved manuscript version and the exact AI model configuration used in each condition; the PDF is undated and Fig. 3c supplies only a gpt-4 workflow label.

For Case Study 1, clarify exclusion timing, randomized/arm counts, and the tested comparison: Fig. 2a places tool introduction between writing tasks, while its caption describes the two tasks more generally.
notes: Screened independently as A. The entire markdown conversion was read, including references; it contains no appendix. The PDF has 25 pages and ends in references. Design/count/result text was checked with PyMuPDF, and Figs. 2-4 were inspected as rendered images in memory; Fig. 3a supplies the 31-story label omitted by markdown/text extraction and Fig. 3c shows gpt-4. Page locators refer to PDF page positions. All three named case studies are retained; the moral study has no eligible creativity outcomes. The headline writing/creativity results and explicitly named rating dimensions are listed separately because their scoring relationships are unspecified; these are not established independent effects. Unknown categorical values lacking a not_stated option are null, including analytical unit and unreported recruitment populations; missing directions are null rather than no_clear_difference. S2 n_units = 31 preserves the figure's stated story count and is not a confirmed t-test sample size. No people counts are derived from outputs or degrees of freedom, and no effect sizes are computed. The largest explicitly reported analyzed human sample is 35 in Case Study 1; counts for Cases 2 and 3 remain unknown. No unassisted post-AI production outcome is described. The repository URL is printed as a hyperlink on p. 18; no direct data URL is supplied and external repository contents were not used. No other screening form was opened.
